item.title: Will Trump’s lame duck presidency push him further beyond constraints of the law?
item.description:
Midterm elections have defanged the US president – leaving critics to worry about his next move in his ‘fat Elvis’ stage

It was just before 3am when Donald Trump entered a crowded Manhattan ballroom, greeted by chants of “USA! USA” and theme music from the Hollywood film Air Force One. On stage, two red “Make America great again” (Maga) caps were mounted in glass cases like holy relics.

That was the scene 10 years ago this week when Trump, a businessman and reality TV star, stunned the world by beating Hillary Clinton to the White House. A decade later an unlikely president is serving an unlikely second term. But in the wake of a humiliating vote of no confidence in last week’s midterm elections, he now enters an endgame wracked with uncertainty.

Continue reading...

item.title: Hegseth survived impeachment bid but reprieve may be temporary: ‘He can’t escape justice forever’
item.description:
The reprimand the defense secretary endured at US military’s most sacred shrine epitomizes his disrepute

The sentinel who bawled out Pete Hegseth for apparent disrespect at the Tomb of the Unknown Solider seemed to be speaking for more than just himself.

Nothing quite epitomizes the disrepute into which the US defense secretary has fallen than the reprimand delivered to Hegseth and his party after they conversed and laughed loudly while visiting Arlington national cemetery on Wednesday to mark Veterans’ Day.
